sourcedFrom: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 (2015)
cleanIntro: A hand-fitted 1911 with a tight match bushing, and Nighthawk's own book carries two instructions that are specific to these guns. ⛔ THE EXTRACTOR COMES OUT EVERY 1,000 TO 2,000 ROUNDS — Nighthawk says carbon build-up in the extractor hole will BREAK the extractor tip, and that breaking it that way voids the warranty on the part. ⛔ AND NEVER LET THE SLIDE DROP ON AN EMPTY CHAMBER: it can make the hammer follow the slide down. The slide should only ever drop on a loaded magazine.

steps.title: Thumb safety ON, magazine caught in your hand
steps.action: Make sure the thumb safety is in the SAFE position. Hold the pistol in your shooting hand with the other hand under the grip to catch the magazine, and fully depress the magazine release.
steps.prose: Nighthawk asks you to catch it rather than let it fall. On a match gun the magazines are fitted parts, and a dropped one lands on its feed lips.
steps.quote: Fully depress the Magazine Release. The Magazine should Slide out of the handgun freely.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEARING THE HANDGUN, printed p.13
steps.warn: Until you pull the Slide back and check for a remaining round in the Chamber, the handgun is still LOADED and capable of firing a round.

steps.title: ⛔ NEVER let the slide fall on an empty chamber
steps.action: With the magazine out, thumb safety to FIRE, draw the slide back and clear the chamber. Then EASE the slide forward — do not release it and let it slam on an empty chamber.
steps.prose: ⛔ Nighthawk's reason is mechanical and specific: it can make the hammer follow the slide down. On a gun with hand-stoned sear surfaces that is a safety problem, not a wear problem. The slide should only ever drop on a loaded magazine.
steps.quote: NEVER RELEASE THE Slide AND LET IT FALL ON AN EMPTY Chamber! This can cause the Hammer to inadvertently follow the Slide down when it closes. The Slide should drop only on a loaded Magazine.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEARING THE HANDGUN, printed p.13

steps.title: ⛔ FIRST: bushing gun or bull-barrel gun?
steps.action: Look at the muzzle. If there is a barrel BUSHING with a closed recoil spring plug inside it, follow the standard strip. If there is no bushing — a bull barrel with a full-length guide rod and a reverse plug — follow the Predator-family strip instead.
steps.prose: ⛔ This decides everything that follows, and it is a two-second look. Nighthawk's own words: the standard procedure is "every model with Standard Barrel / Bushing and Standard Short Guide Rod".
steps.quote: This will be every model with Standard Barrel / Bushing and Standard Short Guide Rod.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21
steps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES AT ALL TIMES. Some parts are under spring tension.

steps.title: ⛔ BUSHING GUN: hold the plug DOWN while the bushing turns
steps.action: Push the guide rod plug down — it is under spring tension — and rotate the bushing until the plug can clear it. ⛔ Keep the plug held down the whole time, and if you are using the bushing wrench, cover the plug the moment the wrench clears it.
steps.prose: ⛔ This is the step that fires a plug across the room, and Nighthawk says so in as many words. The bushings are fitted tight for accuracy, so use the wrench that came in the outside pocket of the pistol bag rather than forcing it by hand.
steps.aside: Nighthawk Barrel Bushings are fit tight for accuracy. Nighthawk Custom recommends using the Barrel Bushing Wrench that is supplied in the outside pocket of your original pistol bag.
steps.quote: PLUG IS UNDER TENSION AND WILL SPRING OUT. AS YOU TURN THE BUSHING, KEEP THE PLUG DOWN.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

steps.title: Slide stop out, slide forward, barrel and bushing out
steps.action: Move the slide back until the rear of the slide stop shows through the slide stop notch, pull the slide stop out, then push the slide and barrel gently forward off the frame. Take the barrel and bushing out of the slide.
steps.prose: That is the field strip. Nighthawk calls it as far down as you need to go for a thorough clean.
steps.aside: You have just completed what is commonly known as "FIELD STRIPPING". This is normally as far down as you need to take your weapon in order to give it a good thorough cleaning.
steps.quote: Move Slide backward until the rear of the Slide Stop is exposed through the Slide Stop Notch on the Slide.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

steps.title: ⛔ BULL-BARREL GUN: capture the spring with the PIN first
steps.action: If there is no bushing: lock the slide back on the slide lock, aim the pistol downward, and put the supplied pin through the hole drilled through the guide rod. Release the slide SLOWLY until the pin captures the recoil spring — there is then no tension left on the slide. Only then pull the slide back, align the slide stop and remove it.
steps.prose: ⛔ The pin came in the box with the pistol for exactly this. Without it the full-length guide rod and reverse plug leave the slide under full spring load.
steps.aside: SLOWLY release the Slide until the Pin captures the Recoil Spring. After performing this, there will be no more tension on the Slide.
steps.quote: The Recoil Spring must be captured in order to remove the Guide Rod successfully. A Pin to capture the Spring was included with your new Nighthawk Custom handgun.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

steps.title: Bull-barrel: guide rod and plug out, then the barrel forward
steps.action: Turn the slide over, roll the barrel link up out of the way and pull the guide rod and reverse plug assembly rearward. Then push the barrel forward and out through the muzzle end.
steps.prose: Link forward first, every time — the link is what catches the barrel in the slide, and forcing it past marks both.
steps.quote: Roll the Barrel Link up out of the way and pull the Guide Rod and Reverse Plug assembly rearward.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

steps.title: Bore and chamber with a properly fitted brush
steps.action: Take the heavy firing residue out of the bore and chamber with a correctly sized brush and solvent, then patch it dry.
steps.prose: "Properly fitted" matters on a match barrel — an oversized brush wedges and an undersized one polishes the fouling instead of removing it.
steps.quote: Remove excessive firing residue from the Bore and Chamber using a properly fitted brush.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.27

steps.title: ⛔ The EXTRACTOR HOOK, every 1,000-2,000 rounds
steps.action: Clean the extractor hook. Nighthawk asks for this roughly every 1,000 to 2,000 rounds — it is not part of every clean, but it is not optional either.
steps.prose: ⛔ The consequence is spelled out: carbon build-up makes the gun fail to extract and can BREAK the extractor tip, and breaking it that way voids the warranty on that part. Cleaning the hole itself needs the firing pin stop out, which is the DEEP CLEAN below.
steps.quote: Be sure to clean your Extractor Hook approximately every 1000-2000 rounds. Failure to do so can cause a carbon build-up which can cause the gun to not extract properly, leading to malfunctions and/or breaking of Extractor, voiding the warranty on that specific part.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.27

steps.title: ⛔ What must never touch a nitride Nighthawk
steps.action: Clean the exterior with a NON-ABRASIVE cloth. ⛔ No trichloroethylene, no ammoniated solvents, no strong alkaline solvents. Avoid solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning.
steps.prose: ⛔ Nighthawk names the finish and the consequence: the black guns wear a nitride/Melonite finish and these chemistries DISCOLOUR it. On a pistol at this price that is a permanent, visible mistake.
steps.aside: You should avoid solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning of your firearm.
steps.quote: Never use cleaning products with Trichloroethylene, ammoniated solvents, or strong alkaline solvents.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.27

steps.title: Light oil inside and out, and no fingerprints
steps.action: After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts — internal and external — with a high-quality gun oil, and take the cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints off the outside surfaces.
steps.prose: Finger moisture starts corrosion. On a blued or nitride finish it shows up as a print-shaped patch weeks later.
steps.quote: After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external with a high-quality gun oil.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete — and reassembly has a trick
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, bushing (or guide rod and reverse plug), recoil spring, plug and slide stop. Reversing it is straightforward with one exception worth knowing.
steps.prose: ⛔ The slide stop must pass through the BARREL LINK as it goes back in. And it has a notch cut in its side that lets it push straight in — using the notch is what stops people levering the slide up or the frame down and scratching both.
steps.quote: Take care to make sure that the Slide Stop passes through the Barrel Link when it is reinserted into the Frame.
steps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — REASSEMBLY, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Eye protection — this spring is under compression
deepSteps.action: Before the firing pin comes out: eye protection on, and point the slide with the firing pin aimed somewhere safe. The pin can leave the slide unexpectedly.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Nighthawk prints this as a CAUTION on its own line. A firing pin is small, hard and travelling at eye height on a bench.
deepSteps.quote: Wear eye protection! This step requires the removal of a spring under compression. Before removing the Firing Pin and Stop, position the Slide with the Firing Pin pointing in a safe direction. The Firing Pin can eject from the Slide unexpectedly and cause injury.
deepSteps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

deepSteps.title: Depress the pin, hold it, then slide the stop off
deepSteps.action: Grasp the rear of the slide and depress the end of the firing pin with a 1/8" punch, far enough to clear the hole in the firing pin stop. Put a finger of the same hand over the firing pin to retain it, then slide the firing pin stop off its rails.
deepSteps.prose: The finger over the pin is what turns this from a two-hand job into a safe one. It is retained by nothing else once the stop moves.
deepSteps.quote: Place a finger of the same hand holding the Slide over the Firing Pin to retain the Firing Pin while removing the Firing Pin Stop.
deepSteps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

deepSteps.title: Pin and spring out, then the extractor
deepSteps.action: Release the pressure on the firing pin slowly and take it out, then take the firing pin spring off by turning the pin clockwise and pulling. With the firing pin stop out, the extractor can come out too.
deepSteps.prose: That is the whole point of getting this far — the extractor and its hole are what needed cleaning, and the firing pin stop is what retains it.
deepSteps.aside: Extractor can be removed after Firing Pin Stop has been removed.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the Firing Pin Spring from the Firing Pin by turning the Firing Pin clockwise and pulling off the Spring.
deepSteps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Clean the extractor HOLE, not just the claw
deepSteps.action: Scrape and brush the carbon out of the extractor hole in the slide as well as off the extractor itself, then wipe both dry before they go back.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Nighthawk's warning is about the hole, not the hook: carbon packed behind the extractor is what stresses the tip until it snaps. The hole is only reachable with the extractor out.
deepSteps.quote: Clean carbon buildup from Extractor Hole and Extractor. The Extractor Tip can break if not cleaned.
deepSteps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

deepSteps.title: ⛔ And if this is past your comfort, Nighthawk says send it
deepSteps.action: If you are not comfortable taking a 1911 down to this level, stop. Nighthawk's own instruction is to send the unloaded pistol to its pistolsmiths for inspection and replacement of worn maintenance parts.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ That is the maker's own offer, printed at the end of its own deepest published procedure. Anything past this point — sear, disconnector, grip safety — is not published for an owner at all.
deepSteps.quote: If you are not comfortable taking your 1911 down to this level, you can also choose to send your unloaded pistol to Nighthawk Custom Pistolsmiths for an inspection and replacement of any worn maintenance parts.
deepSteps.cite: Nighthawk Custom Handgun Safety & Reference Owner's Manual — Nighthawk-Safety-Manual-2015-03 — HANDGUN MAINTENANCE - DISASSEMBLY, printed pp.16-21

cleaning.name: BARREL & BUSHING
tasks: Properly fitted brush and solvent, bore and chamber
Bushing inner face — it is a bearing surface on a match gun
Patch dry, then a light oil film

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Breech face and the extractor claw every clean
⛔ Non-abrasive cloth only on a nitride finish

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Rails, disconnector track and magazine well
Light high-quality gun oil, internal and external
Fingerprints wiped off — finger moisture starts corrosion

cleaning.name: CHEMISTRY
tasks: ⛔ No trichloroethylene, ammonia or strong alkali
⛔ No solvent immersion, no prolonged ultrasonic
Cold-climate use needs an oil that will not congeal

reassembly: Reverse the strip for whichever configuration your pistol is.
⛔ Make sure the slide stop passes through the BARREL LINK as it goes back into the frame.
Use the notch cut into the side of the slide stop to push it straight in — it forces the plunger tube pin back progressively instead of you levering on the slide or frame.
On a bushing gun, hold the plug down and rotate the bushing back over it.
On a bull-barrel gun, the capture pin comes out only once the guide rod assembly is seated.
fncheck: Unloaded and proven, empty magazine only, muzzle safe. Rack the slide by hand several times — a hand-fitted gun should be smooth, not notchy — and check the barrel returns fully into battery. With the hammer cocked, apply the thumb safety: the slide should lock and the trigger should be dead. Off safe, grip it properly and dry-fire once; repeat WITHOUT depressing the grip safety and the hammer must NOT fall. ⛔ Then ease the slide down on an empty chamber rather than dropping it, and check the extractor hook is clean and its tip undamaged.
